transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-04 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Daniel Cruz (Redwood SE), Oliver Park (Rosetta Head of ML), Priya Sharma (Rosetta CTO), Marcus Lee (Rosetta Infra), Sofia Ruiz (Rosetta Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
- Check-in focused on renewal options and APAC burst capacity.
- Customer wants predictable commit with ability to burst for seasonal inference spikes.
- Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private (VPC/on-prem) tradeoffs, KMS, SOC2, SSO.
- Next steps: pricing scenarios, benchmark run, security docs, contract amendment planning.

Topics: renewal sizing, APAC region activation, latency SLOs, cost tradeoffs, contract term options, security compliance, pilot timeline

Action items (captured):
- Maya to send pricing scenarios and amended SOW template.
- Daniel to run performance baseline on APAC cluster with Rosetta prompts.
- Marcus to share infra and QPS numbers.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Lin: Hey everybody, thanks for jumping on. I think we've got about 45 minutes. Quick check — is this still the right agenda, renewals and APAC burst planning?
[00:07] Oliver Park: Yeah that's right. Thanks, Maya. We wanted to nail down the committed numbers and make sure the APAC burst is actually supported with acceptable latency.
[00:14] Priya Sharma: And to add, we need the contract extended through Q2 next year ideally, but open to options if the economics look good.
[00:20] Maya Lin: Great. I can walk through two scenarios, committed reserve with burst credits, or a staggered ramp where you commit a base and buy additional reserved top-ups. Daniel, want to chime on latency expectations in APAC?
[00:31] Daniel Cruz: Sure. High level: hosted Redwood API in apac-east should give p50s in the low 100s ms for our Llama-style variants at your typical seq lengths, p95 will be higher especially under burst. If you need sub-100ms we should talk Dedicated in a region or edge nodes. Also, caching/prefix reuse will help — but depends on your prompt mix.
[00:52] Marcus Lee: When you say low 100s, is that cold start or warmed? We have a lot of short chat queries so cold start hurts.
[00:59] Daniel Cruz: Those are warmed steady-state numbers. Cold start for new sessions could add 100-300ms depending on model. We can do prefix caching or pool warm VMs for your agent sessions to mitigate.
[01:12] Sofia Ruiz: Sorry to interrupt — what's the delta in cost if we go Dedicated vs Hosted?
[01:17] Maya Lin: Rough ballpark — Dedicated committed pools lock you into monthly units, so unit token cost tends to be 20-40% lower depending on the model and utilization you hit. Hosted is more flexible but unit cost higher; burst credits on Hosted cost a premium. We'll send exact math in the pricing sheet.
[01:31] Oliver Park: Our main constraint is predictability of spend and guarantees for latency during peak events. We have a product launch window in September so want staging in APAC earlier.
[01:43] Priya Sharma: Also, we have compliance constraints — SOC 2 is mandatory and KMS integration for certain datasets. Does Redwood Private support customer-managed keys for on-prem or VPC?
[01:54] Daniel Cruz: Yes — for Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations. For Dedicated we can also bring KMS integrations via VPC peering and client-side encryption. We'll share the integration notes, but technically it's supported.
[02:08] Marcus Lee: Ok good. On the network side, our tenancy will be peered and we can expose metrics, but we need an SLO for p95 under committed load. Can Redwood commit to a p95 SLO for dedicated nodes?
[02:22] Maya Lin: We do provide SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated tiers. Exact numbers depend on the commitment level and model family. For commitments above X units we can include a p95 latency SLO in the contract. I'll follow up with the thresholds in writing.
[02:36] Oliver Park: Cool. Can we talk about scaling — how fast can you spin up capacity in APAC if we increase commit mid-year?
[02:44] Daniel Cruz: Our autoscaling for Dedicated is policy-driven; there is an activation lead time for additional reserved capacity — typically 2-4 weeks for guaranteed reserved provisioning. For Hosted burst, you can immediately hit the public API but with higher cost and possible throttling if regional capacity is constrained.
[03:00] Priya Sharma: That 2-4 week window is a bit long for our ops — any way to shorten it?
[03:05] Maya Lin: We offer a fast-provisioning add-on (expedited capacity) for customers that need quicker ramp for a fee. Also we can plan a buffer — e.g., keep a small extra reserved pool that you only pay minimal carry for. We'll include both options in the pricing scenarios.
[03:20] Marcus Lee: For the pilot, we want a baseline test with our prompt set and QPS profile. Daniel, can you run p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens in APAC and US for our model mix?
[03:31] Daniel Cruz: Yep I can run that. Send the sample prompts and expected sequence lengths; I'll spin a 1-hour run. If the sample corpus is representative we'll get realistic p95 numbers and cost extrapolation.
[03:42] Sofia Ruiz: We'll upload a 1k prompt test set to the shared drive after the call.
[03:46] Maya Lin: Perfect. We'll use that for the benchmark.
[03:50] Oliver Park: On contract length — we prefer 12 months but open to 6 months with a renewal clause if the economics are right. Priya?
[03:58] Priya Sharma: 12 months is preferable because it gives predictability, but we want the ability to add geo capacity mid-term without renegotiating the base.
[04:08] Maya Lin: We can draft an amendment language that allows add-on capacity to be purchased without changing the primary term, and list lead times and pricing. That will probably be a schedule to the master SOW.
[04:18] Priya Sharma: That sounds good. Also, are there limits on model variants when you do burst? For example, if we pin to a quantized 8-bit variant for cost, can you serve both 8-bit and full models as fallback?
[04:31] Daniel Cruz: Yes, smart routing/fallback is supported. We can route to a compatible variant automatically when higher-tier instances are saturated, or to a more quantized profile if you're comfortable with marginal quality degradation. We'll outline the exact model variant compatibility matrix.
[04:47] Marcus Lee: A note on telemetry — we want token-level cost breakdowns per route and per model so our finance team can attribute spend. Is that available?
[04:55] Maya Lin: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency breakdowns per model/route and you can export reports. We'll include an example export.
[05:05] Oliver Park: Security-wise, beyond SOC 2 and KMS, we need audit logs for requests and access, and SSO via SAML.
[05:12] Daniel Cruz: Those are standard. SAML SSO, RBAC, audit logs are part of our enterprise feature set. For Private you'll get extended retention options for logs as well.
[05:22] Sofia Ruiz: One question: if we move to Private (on-prem), how much engineering effort on our side are we looking at?
[05:28] Daniel Cruz: For on-prem it's a collaborative effort — typically 4-6 weeks of integration depending on network and hardware availability. We'll provide an on-prem checklist. If you already have GPUs and k8s infra it shortens the timeline.
[05:40] Priya Sharma: Our infra team prefers VPC first, then consider on-prem later. So VPC + KMS would be the likely route.
[05:48] Maya Lin: Makes sense. We'll prioritize VPC playbook + KMS notes.
[05:52] Oliver Park: Ok for payments, we use PO + net 45. Any constraint on that?
[05:58] Maya Lin: That's standard for many customers. For committed capacity contracts we sign SOW + PO and work with finance. We can include net terms in the amendment.
[06:06] Marcus Lee: Can you also confirm data retention and whether logs can be redacted or hashed for PII?
[06:12] Daniel Cruz: Yes, we have data retention policies and can enable redaction for sensitive logs; we'll send the retention matrix and redaction options.
[06:20] Priya Sharma: Great. Timeline check — we want the APAC staging to begin late June so we can run a closed beta in July before the September launch. Is that feasible with the provisioning lead times you mentioned?
[06:33] Daniel Cruz: If we commit this month and you sign the SOW, we can stage a small Dedicated pilot in APAC by mid-June (if expedited provisioning is purchased) otherwise late June is doable for smaller pools. We'll include the calendar in the write-up.
[06:46] Maya Lin: To summarize next steps — we'll send two pricing scenarios and SOW amendment language, Daniel will run the performance baseline once you upload the prompt set, and Marcus will share infra details. We'll also attach SOC 2 and KMS integration notes.
[06:58] Oliver Park: Perfect. Any lingering concerns from the team?
[07:03] Sofia Ruiz: One small one — does Redwood support region-level failover for customers if APAC has an outage?
[07:09] Daniel Cruz: Yes, we have smart routing and fallback to other regions as a grace measure, but failover adds cross-region latency; we'd recommend active-active architecture in critical paths. We'll document the tradeoffs.
[07:21] Priya Sharma: Ok thanks, that addresses most things.
[07:24] Maya Lin: Thanks everyone. We'll aim to get the materials out by Friday.

(There are intermittent transcription artifacts below — some words misrecognized by the auto-transcriber)
